subject: Computer Networking
title: Site Surveys and Heat Maps
description: Learn Site Surveys and Heat Maps in one minute.

hook.text: Before installing APs, engineers walk the building with a laptop. They're making a Wi-Fi heat map.

buildup.text: A site survey measures signal strength, noise, and interference. Software turns data into a color map.

discovery.text: Red zones have strong signal. Blue zones are weak. The map shows exactly where to place APs.

twist.text: Walls, metal, water, and people absorb Wi-Fi. A pretty floor plan can be a terrible radio environment.

climax.text: Predictive surveys simulate AP placement before install. Optimize coverage without drilling a hole.

punchline.text: A heat map turns Wi-Fi guesswork into precise engineering.

quiz.question: What does a Wi-Fi site survey measure?
options: Signal strength, noise, and interference at each location
The number of devices connected to each AP
The internet speed from the ISP

details.summary: Site surveys measure wireless signal strength, interference, and coverage throughout a physical space to plan optimal access point placement. Heat maps visualize this data as color-coded overlays on floor plans, revealing dead zones, channel conflicts, and areas needing additional coverage.
details.whyItMatters: Deploying Wi-Fi without a site survey leads to dead spots, interference, and wasted budget on too many or poorly placed access points. Surveys ensure reliable coverage from the start.
takeaways: Site surveys map signal strength across a physical space
Heat maps reveal dead zones and interference visually
Predictive surveys can model coverage before installation

faq.question: What tools are used for Wi-Fi site surveys?
faq.answer: Professional tools like Ekahau and NetSpot walk the surveyor through the space, measuring signal strength, noise, and throughput at each point. The software generates heat maps overlaid on floor plans. Spectrum analyzers detect non-Wi-Fi interference from microwaves, Bluetooth, and other sources.

faq.question: What is a predictive site survey?
faq.answer: Predictive surveys use software to simulate wireless coverage based on floor plan dimensions and wall materials without physically visiting the site. They are faster and cheaper than on-site surveys but less accurate.
